newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa reverses as NY eases.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa reverses as NY eases.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa surrendered earlier shortcovering-related gains to end Tuesday narrowly mixed after the New York equivalent market retraced sharply from Monday's run-up.
At the close, LIFFE benchmark Sept was down one stg at 1,017 stg a tonne after a high of 1,028. Its low point was 1,010.
But December was one stg higher at 1,054. Volume was 4,050 lots. Traders said turnover was thin on the way up and down.
Trade and origin selling was also seen.
New York cocoa futures, which ended up sharply and near the day's highs on Monday, came under heavy speculative selling to head lower.
Some dealers viewed today's downturn to a technical correction to an overbought condition.

On the fundamental front, Economist Intelligence Unit on Tuesday lowered its 1996/97 world cocoa deficit estimate to 85,000 tonnes from 200,000 tonnes previously due to higher-than-expected production.
Cocoa posted a supply surplus of 160,000 tonnes in the 1995/96 season, it said.
In its third quarter 1997 world commodity forecasts, EIU put the supply cocoa deficit at 73,000 tonnes in 1997/98 and 18,000 in 1998/99.
In physical news, Ivorian cocoa bean exports fell to 21,841 tonnes in June from 34,966 in May as port deliveries remained slack after the main crop season (Oct-April), official shipping data show.
